chapter: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
title: Old horns versus new: metal, workmanship and salesmanship
summary: He thinks old instruments sound better because of purer metal, comparing them to a Rolls-Royce versus a Ford.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Speaking of that sort of thing, has the quality of instruments improved during the time that you've been playing?

I think that the quality... Well, maybe it's the workmanship, but the metal just don't seem as nice and sturdy as it used to. I guess everybody's trying to save something. You know? But the metal of those old instruments... That's why an old instrument sounds good, because the metal is... They made it with purer things, you know. Good... And the workmanship is good, too. Of course, there have been improvements. They put things on the assembly line sort of stuff now. It's just like you get a Rolls-Royce which is hand-built, and get a Ford which has gone through the thing, you know. You've got something worth something when you've got the Rolls-Royce right, and it's always going to be worth something. And that's the way with an old horn and a new horn. Especially if they ain't got smashed up or something... But still, that metal is great that they used...
Though it seems to me that when you look at old band pictures, things have changed, like the size of the bell and some of these...
Well, yeah. They've been improving things and they do things...

It's for salesmanship a lot. A lot of it is for salesmanship. Like, some trombones, they used to put those slanty-looking things on it to make it look streamlined and all that stuff. But it wasn't no different than any other horn right on... I mean, the sound is what you've got to think about. It isn't the looks of it. It's the sound that you get out of a horn. And it seems like the horns with the old metals seem to be more... I don't know what to say. They sound better. Control...
